chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Al-wadhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution); it is only like nasal mucus and spittle.

key_terms.الْوَذْيُ: A bodily discharge referred to in the hadith, ruled here as not nullifying wudu (ablution).
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: Wudu (ablution), the ritual washing required for certain acts of worship.
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the status or category of; treated as equivalent to.
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: Invalidates or breaks a state of ritual purity.

ai.seo_question: Does al-wadhy invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that al-wadhy does not invalidate wudu (ablution). It classifies it alongside ordinary bodily substances such as nasal mucus and saliva, indicating ritual purity is not broken by it.
